title: Behind the same story
intro: The same patient and the same twelve steps, seen from underneath: the audit trail, the agent gateway, the validator, the evals and the workflow.

end.title: Every number here comes from the app's own trace store and eval files.
end.text: Mock-model runs are baselines that prove the pipeline, not clinical performance. All data is synthetic.

steps.caption: Each step records three things: what the AI proposed, who signed, and the audit events. Step 1: the registration the agent pre-filled, confirmed by Maya Nakamura.
The audit log is append-only and SHA-256 hash-chained. Each event says who, which role, when, which record and why; the patient appears only as a keyed hash.

steps.screen: AI Ops · an agent run's trace
steps.caption: Every agent run leaves a trace: model and prompt version, on whose behalf it ran, inputs and outputs, its FHIR Provenance, and the human decision that followed.

steps.screen: AI Ops · an agent run's trace
steps.caption: Each tool call passes the gateway with a side-effect level. The gateway authorises from the registry and the signed-in caller, never from what the model claims.
Every agent and module is registered with a risk tier (ops, documentation, clinical decision support) and the role that must sign. The registry decides, not the screen.
Second axis: tools by side effect (read, recommend, action, privileged). An ops agent can reach a privileged tool, like a bed move; that call still needs a recorded approval.
Each line carries references to FHIR resources. Select a line and the source panel highlights what it cites, here her home warfarin, so every claim can be checked.
The validator is deterministic code, not another model. A medicine with no matching order turns red, and the signing service refuses the draft by any path, not just this button.
One command runs every agent's eval set against its threshold. Mock-model runs are baselines: they prove the pipeline and never pass the release gate on their own.
Prompts are versioned files. Change one without an eval run that meets the agent's threshold, and the prompt gate fails the test suite.
Her stay is one durable Temporal workflow: sign-offs are signals, the 48-hour follow-up is a timer. Kill the worker mid-step and it resumes without repeating a side effect.
steps.note: Captured locally with Temporal on; the public demo runs without Temporal (offline mode).
